import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_2.csv"

df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source3_25_1", "Source3_25_2"], ["movie_id", "movie_id"]]
# 2) JOIN : [["Source3_25_0", "Source3_25_1"], ["user_id", "user_id"]]

# Step 1: Join Source3_25_1 and Source3_25_2 on movie_id
df_join_1 = pd.merge(df_source1, df_source2, how='inner', on='movie_id')

# Step 2: Join Source3_25_0 and the result of previous join on user_id
df_join_2 = pd.merge(df_source0, df_join_1, how='inner', on='user_id')

# Now select and reorder columns to match the target schema:
# Target Schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Convert columns to the target types:
# - title: string (already string)
# - user_id: float
# - movie_id: integer
# - rating: float
# - timestamp: float
# - age: float
# - occupation: float

# Prepare final DataFrame with correct columns and types
df_target = pd.DataFrame()

df_target['title'] = df_join_2['title'].astype(str)
df_target['user_id'] = df_join_2['user_id'].astype(float)
df_target['movie_id'] = df_join_2['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_target['rating'] = df_join_2['rating'].astype(float)
df_target['timestamp'] = df_join_2['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_target['age'] = df_join_2['age'].astype(float)
df_target['occupation'] = df_join_2['occupation'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 with the above result on user_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by title, user_id, movie_id (leftmost non-float columns in target schema)
# Aggregate rating, timestamp, age, occupation by average
result = joined_all.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
